body: The Last Guy is Japan Studio's PlayStation 3 rescue game, released on 28 August 2008. Viewed from high above monster-infested cities, the player gathers stranded civilians into a following line and guides them towards safety before time expires. The leader is small against the city, making the route more important than a heroic close-up. Every rescued person adds to the group that must be brought through the streets. A useful shortcut for one character may be less safe once a long crowd is trailing behind, turning rescue into a problem of shape and movement.

Thermal imaging helps locate survivors, while dashing and controlling the line provide tools for moving them around threats. The player has to judge when to gather a larger crowd and when to deliver those already following. A monster can make a familiar street dangerous, so the route must remain open to revision. Special VIPs offer extra rewards and can unlock further stages, encouraging attention beyond the most obvious groups. The task is readable from a distance: identify a stranded population, form a manageable line and bring it to the place where the city can finally be left behind.

The playable locations draw on cities across North America, Europe and Asia, using the overhead view to make buildings and streets part of a maze. Leaderboards and rescue totals give completed stages another reason to be revisited. The digital release followed a Japan-only preview and later received trophy support and additional downloadable material. Its distinctive effect comes from the distance of the camera. Individual figures are tiny, but the line accumulating behind the player makes the scale of a successful rescue visible, turning a growing crowd into both the reward and the responsibility carried through the level.
